description: Fetch content from a URL and convert HTML pages into clean Markdown.
name: web_fetch

start.description: Character offset to read from, to page through (default 0).

url.description: The HTTP or HTTPS URL to fetch.

description: Perform a web search and return structured title, URL, and snippet results.
name: web_search

max_results.description: Maximum number of search results to return (default: 5).

description: List the tools available to you in this session, optionally filtered by a keyword (matched against names and descriptions). Use it when a call fails with 'no tool named ...' or when you are unsure what exists, instead of guessing a name.
name: search_tools

query.description: Keyword to look for, e.g. 'github' or 'file'. Empty lists all.

description: Load tools listed under 'Tools to load before use' so you can call them: their definitions are added from your next step and stay for the rest of the session. Load every tool you expect to need in one call.
name: load_tools

description: Prompt the human user with a structured single- or multi-choice decision card when user intent is underspecified, requirements conflict, or multiple valid architectural trade-offs exist (e.g. library choice, breaking API changes, destructive actions). Always provide clear, distinct options with a recommended default. In the Web Cockpit and Slack, this renders an interactive button/radio decision card and pauses the turn until the user makes a selection.
name: ask_question

is_multi_select.description: Whether multiple options can be chosen (default: false).

options.description: List of selectable options for the user.

description: Rename the current session with a concise, descriptive title (3-6 words) reflecting the topic.
name: session_rename

title.description: The new concise, descriptive title for the session.

description: Record an explicit reasoning checkpoint (scratchpad) before the next action. The checkpoint is surfaced to the user as a reasoning event.
name: think

description: Create or update the task checklist the user follows. Every call REPLACES the whole list, so always send all tasks. Use it for work with three or more steps: create it first, keep exactly one task in_progress, and mark each task completed as soon as it is done, not later. Before your final answer no task may stay pending or in_progress: mark finished work completed and abandoned work failed. Send an empty list to clear it when it no longer helps. Call it only when a task's status changes, never on every step.
name: update_task_checklist

tasks.description: List of tasks in the checklist.

title.description: Short human-readable title of the task.

description: Delegate an isolated investigation or task to a specialist subagent (e.g. security_auditor, qa_verifier, researcher, or any custom role configured by the organization).
name: delegate_subagent

context.description: Optional background hints or specific files to inspect.

role.description: Specialist role to spawn (e.g. 'security_auditor', 'qa_verifier', 'researcher', or custom organization specialist).

task.description: Clear, specific objective for the subagent to accomplish.

description: Delegate multiple specialized subagents to execute tasks concurrently or sequentially. Parallel write subagents require >= 2 CPU and >= 4 GiB RAM; if the sandbox profile is smaller, delegations run sequentially to prevent memory exhaustion.
name: delegate_subagents_parallel

description: Enter read-only plan mode. Use for multi-step or risky work: investigate safely, then present a plan before changing anything.
name: enter_plan_mode

description: Leave plan mode and request human approval for the proposed plan.
name: exit_plan_mode

summary.description: Concise summary of the plan requiring approval.

description: Ask the human to approve a sensitive or destructive action (force push, hard reset, data deletion, costly external call) before performing it.
name: request_approval

description.description: What will happen and why it is needed.

description: Create a durable session artifact (specifications, architecture documents, migration plans, diff reports, diagrams, or JSON deliverables). Artifacts are stored in the session control plane, readable by the user in the Cockpit Artifacts drawer independently of sandbox pod lifecycles, and save LLM context window by replacing large outputs with lightweight receipts.
name: create_artifact

content.description: The complete text/code content of the artifact.

description: Update an existing session artifact with new content, incrementing its version.
name: update_artifact

artifact_id.description: The unique artifact ID to update.

description: Retrieve the content of a previously created session artifact by its ID.
name: read_artifact

description: List all durable artifacts created in the current session.
name: list_artifacts

description: Search PostgreSQL pgvector knowledge bases for semantic documentation, architecture guides, and API specs.
name: kb_search

kb_id.description: Optional specific knowledge base ID to scope search.

query.description: Natural language question or search query.

description: Persist a durable fact, preference, decision or convention for future sessions. Use it deliberately for knowledge worth keeping across sessions; never store secrets or credentials (they are refused).
name: remember

content.description: The durable statement to remember, in one clear sentence.

scope.description: Who the memory applies to (default: user).

description: Search durable long-term memories relevant to a query and return the best matches. Use it before answering questions about past decisions, conventions or preferences.
name: recall

query.description: Natural-language description of what to remember.

scope.description: Optional scope to restrict the search to.

description: Load or run a skill from the organization's library (the available names are listed under [Skills] in your instructions). An instruction skill returns its full instructions for you to follow; a code skill runs with the given arguments. Call it before starting work the skill covers.
name: execute_skill

arguments.description: Arguments for a code skill; pass {} for an instruction skill.

skill_name.description: Name of the skill, exactly as listed under [Skills].

description: Clone a GitHub repository into the sandbox at /workspace/<name> and describe it (branch, last commit, top-level files). The sandbox starts BLANK: nothing is checked out until you clone it, and many tasks need no repository at all. When one is needed, find it first (user's request, `kb_search`, skills, `github_find_repositories`), then clone. Idempotent: an existing clone is refreshed. Authentication is automatic. A fresh clone's result includes the repository's own AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md: follow it.
name: clone_repository

branch.description: Branch to check out (default: the default branch).

depth.description: Only the latest N commits, for very large repositories (default: full history, file contents fetched on demand).

directory.description: Folder name under /workspace (default: the repository name).

description: Make another cloned repository the active one: git, test and build tools and relative file paths use it when you name no folder, in this turn and later ones. Not needed to run a command elsewhere: `bash_exec` takes its folder as `cwd`, and the other tools take `path`.
name: set_active_repository

path.description: The repository's folder, e.g. /workspace/api.

description: Follow a pull request (or a branch) so this session hears about it: CI results, reviews, comments, merge or close. Use it to wait for CI or a review without polling or building a tool. Events reach you in a later turn on their own; a pull request you open with git_open_pr is followed automatically. Following stops by itself when the pull request is merged or closed.
name: github_watch

branch.description: Follow CI on this branch instead (no pull request).

wake.description: Start a turn when something happens (default); false only records events for your next turn.

description: Stop following a pull request or branch (all of a repository's if neither is given).
name: github_unwatch

description: Find GitHub repositories without a sandbox: by owner/organization (its most recently active repositories), by search text, or - with neither - those the user's credential can see. Use it to work out which repository a task refers to before cloning.
name: github_find_repositories

owner.description: A user or organization to restrict to.

query.description: Words from the name or description.

description: Read one file, or list a directory, of a GitHub repository WITHOUT cloning or starting a sandbox (README, AGENTS.md, a config file, the repository root). Use it to understand a repository before deciding to clone it. Once the repository is cloned in the sandbox, do NOT use this: read and search the local files with `file_read`, `list_dir` and `grep_search` (faster, and they include your own changes).
name: github_read_file

path.description: File or directory path; empty lists the root.

description: GitHub issues (what `gh issue` does). Read: pass `number` for one issue or pull request with its description and latest comments, `query` to search, or neither to list the latest. Change (action): create (title, body, labels, assignees), comment, edit, close, reopen.
name: github_issues

action.description: A change to make; leave empty to read.

description: Inspect all repositories in the workspace, detect inter-repo dependencies, write/update /workspace/.rocket/workspace.json, and return a structured summary table.
name: workspace_status

refresh.description: Whether to force re-scanning every repository from disk.

scan_dependencies.description: Whether to scan package manifests for inter-repository dependencies.

description: Return porcelain git status across all repositories in the workspace, highlighting branches and dirty worktrees.
name: git_status_all

only_dirty.description: If True, only show repositories with uncommitted changes or untracked files.

description: Execute a command across every repository in the workspace (or a subset), aggregating clamped output and status codes per repository.
name: repo_foreach

command.description: Shell command to run in each repository.

fail_fast.description: Stop executing if any repository command returns non-zero.

repos.description: Comma-separated repository names to target (default: all).

description: Work with pull requests. Send a list of actions to run in order. Reads: list, view, files, diff (paged by file), checks, review_threads. Writes: edit (title/body/base), ready, draft, request_reviewers, comment, review (event comment|request_changes|approve), reply_to_thread (comment_id), resolve_thread (thread_id), close, reopen, merge. Open a PR with git_open_pr.
name: github_pull_request

actions.description: What to do. Multiple actions run in order (e.g. ['view','comments','checks']).

body.description: Text: comment, review, reply or new description.

page.description: Page of files for diff (10 files a page).

description: GitHub Actions (what `gh run` does). Read: runs (optionally on a branch), run_view (its jobs and failed steps), job_logs (the end of a job's log, where failures are). Change: rerun_failed, cancel, dispatch_workflow (workflow + ref + inputs).
name: github_actions

ref.description: Branch or tag to run on (dispatch).

description: GitHub releases (what `gh release` does): list, view (by tag), create or edit (tag_name, name, body, draft, prerelease, target_commitish).
name: github_releases

description: Search GitHub (what `gh search` does): code, issues (and pull requests) or commits, optionally within one repository. Uses GitHub search syntax.
name: github_search

description: Any other GitHub REST or GraphQL call (what `gh api` does), when no dedicated github_* tool covers it. REST: method + path (e.g. GET /repos/o/r/branches), query, body, paginate. GraphQL: graphql (+ variables; a mutation needs repository). Reads need no approval; changes follow the permission mode, DELETE always asks. Secrets, keys, webhooks, protection, access and administration are refused.
name: github_api

method.description: GET, POST, PATCH, PUT or DELETE.

path.description: REST path, e.g. /repos/o/r/labels.

description: Read a file with line numbers, 400 lines at a time unless you give a range; the result says how many lines the file has and how to read on. The numbers are not part of the file: leave them out of file_edit blocks.
name: file_read

line_numbers.description: Prefix each line with its number (default: true).

path.description: File to read. Relative paths are inside the active repository; absolute ones as given.

description: Write or overwrite file contents in the sandbox workspace.
name: file_write

overwrite.description: Whether to overwrite existing file (default: true).

path.description: File to create or overwrite. Relative paths are inside the active repository; absolute ones as given.

description: Perform resilient block replacement in a workspace file.
name: file_edit

path.description: File to edit. Relative paths are inside the active repository; absolute ones as given.

target_block.description: Exact or near-exact block of lines to replace.

description: Apply a unified diff patch to a file in the workspace.
name: apply_patch

path.description: File to patch. Relative paths are inside the active repository; absolute ones as given.

description: Apply only one file's hunks from a multi-file unified diff to the workspace, after human approval. Use it to accept a single file of a proposed multi-file patch.
name: apply_diff_file

diff_content.description: The full unified diff, possibly spanning several files.

path.description: Workspace-relative file to apply from the diff.

description: List the contents of a directory in the sandbox workspace (long format).
name: list_dir

path.description: Directory to list (default: '.'). Relative paths are inside the active repository; absolute ones as given.

description: Search file contents recursively for a regex pattern (ripgrep, with grep fallback). Prefer this over bash grep/find for repository navigation.
name: grep_search

case_sensitive.description: Whether the search is case sensitive (default: true).

path.description: Directory or file to search within (default: '.').

description: Find workspace files matching a glob pattern (supports ** recursion).
name: glob_files

path.description: Root directory to search from (default: '.').

description: Search the codebase for symbols (functions, classes, types) matching a name or term. Prefer this for 'where is X defined' questions.
name: code_search

path.description: Directory to search from (default: '.').

description: Execute a shell command inside the sandbox, in bash (sh only in an image without bash). Each call is a fresh shell: `cd` and `export` do not carry over. Always say where it runs with `cwd`; never start the command with `cd`. For variables every command needs, use `env_set` once instead of exporting them each time.
name: bash_exec

command.description: The shell command to execute, without `cd`.

cwd.description: Folder to run in, e.g. /workspace/api (absolute, or relative to /workspace).

description: Install or manage project dependencies through the workspace's declared package manager (uv, pnpm, npm or poetry). Lockfile-aware; returns a parsed failure cause when an install fails.
name: package_manager

dev.description: Add as a development dependency (add only).

manager.description: Explicit package manager override (auto-detected if omitted).

packages.description: Package names to add or remove (e.g. ['pytest', 'ruff']).

path.description: Project folder, e.g. 'my-app' or 'my-app/packages/api'. Default: the session's active repository, or the only repository under /workspace.

description: Run the project test suite, auto-detecting npm/cargo/go/pytest, and return a parsed pass/fail summary. Use this to verify changes before finishing.
name: run_tests

command.description: Optional explicit test command overriding detection.

path.description: Project folder, e.g. 'my-app' or 'my-app/packages/api'. Default: the session's active repository, or the only repository under /workspace.

description: Run the project linter (auto-detects npm/ruff/clippy/go vet/make).
name: lint

command.description: Optional explicit lint command overriding detection.

path.description: Project folder, e.g. 'my-app' or 'my-app/packages/api'. Default: the session's active repository, or the only repository under /workspace.

description: Run the project type checker (auto-detects npm/mypy/tsc/cargo/go).
name: typecheck

command.description: Optional explicit typecheck command overriding detection.

path.description: Project folder, e.g. 'my-app' or 'my-app/packages/api'. Default: the session's active repository, or the only repository under /workspace.

description: Build the project (auto-detects npm/python/cargo/go/make).
name: build

command.description: Optional explicit build command overriding detection.

path.description: Project folder, e.g. 'my-app' or 'my-app/packages/api'. Default: the session's active repository, or the only repository under /workspace.

description: Open a page in a headless browser inside the sandbox and report what a person would see: title, page structure, visible text, console errors and failed requests. Use it to check an app you started (for example http://localhost:3000/) instead of guessing.
name: browser_inspect

screenshot.description: Also save a screenshot to the workspace (default: false).

wait_ms.description: Extra time to let the page settle, in ms (default: 500).

description: Look at an image file from the workspace (a screenshot, a diagram, a design). The image is shown to you with your next step; it needs a model that can see images, and says so if yours cannot. Formats: PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, up to 5 MB. Use it to check a UI you built or to read a screenshot instead of guessing.
name: view_image

path.description: Image path inside /workspace.

description: Set an environment variable for every later command of this session (bash_exec, tests, builds, background processes), in this and later turns. Use it instead of exporting the same variable in each command, e.g. GOPRIVATE or NODE_OPTIONS.
name: env_set

description: Remove a variable you set with env_set.
name: env_unset

description: List the variables set for every command: the ones you set with env_set (with their values) and the sandbox type's (names only).
name: env_list

description: Start a long-running command in the BACKGROUND (a dev server, a watcher, a slow build) and return at once with a process id. `bash_exec` blocks until its command ends and kills it on timeout, so use this for anything that keeps running. Declare `port` for a server: the person can then open it in the Preview tab. Read output with `process_output`, wait for it to finish with `process_wait`, stop it with `process_stop`. Processes end when the sandbox is hibernated; the session is told about any that exited while you were away.
name: process_start

command.description: The shell command to run in the background.

name.description: Short label shown to the person (default: the command).

port.description: TCP port the process serves on, if any.

description: List the background processes of this session and their state.
name: process_list

description: Read the latest output (stdout and stderr together) of a background process.
name: process_output

description: Wait until a background process ends (or the timeout passes) and return its exit code and last output. Use it for builds and test runs started with process_start.
name: process_wait

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait, at most 300 (default 60).

description: Stop a background process and everything it started.
name: process_stop

description: Alias for process_start: launch a command as a detached background task.
name: task_start

command.description: The shell command to run in the background.

name.description: Short label shown to the user (default: the command).

description: Alias for process_list: list active background tasks.
name: task_list

description: Alias for process_output: read output or check status of a background task.
name: task_status

lines.description: How many trailing lines of output to read.

task_id.description: Task id returned by task_start or process_start.

description: Alias for process_stop: cancel or terminate a running background task.
name: task_kill

task_id.description: Task id returned by task_start or process_start.

description: Return the porcelain git status (current branch + changed/untracked files) of a repository.
name: git_status

path.description: Repository folder, e.g. 'my-app' for /workspace/my-app. Default: the session's active repository (the first one cloned), or the only repository under /workspace.

description: Show the current unified git diff (optionally staged, scoped to a file, or stat-only).
name: git_diff

file.description: Optional file, relative to the repository, to scope the diff to.

path.description: Repository folder, e.g. 'my-app' for /workspace/my-app. Default: the session's active repository (the first one cloned), or the only repository under /workspace.

stat_only.description: Return only a diffstat summary (default: false).

description: Return structured git history: author, date, subject and changed files per commit.
name: git_log

file.description: Optional file or folder to scope the history to.

path.description: Repository folder, e.g. 'my-app' for /workspace/my-app. Default: the session's active repository (the first one cloned), or the only repository under /workspace.

description: Commit every change in a repository, following the organization's authorship and signing policy (co-author trailers included). Prefer a checkpoint first for destructive work.
name: git_commit

branch.description: Optional branch to create/checkout before committing.

path.description: Repository folder, e.g. 'my-app' for /workspace/my-app. Default: the session's active repository (the first one cloned), or the only repository under /workspace.

description: Create and switch to a new git branch.
name: git_branch

from_ref.description: Optional base commit/branch to branch from.

path.description: Repository folder, e.g. 'my-app' for /workspace/my-app. Default: the session's active repository (the first one cloned), or the only repository under /workspace.

description: Snapshot a repository, uncommitted work included, as a restorable checkpoint. Cheap undo point before large or risky edits.
name: git_checkpoint

path.description: Repository folder, e.g. 'my-app' for /workspace/my-app. Default: the session's active repository (the first one cloned), or the only repository under /workspace.

description: Restore a repository to a checkpoint or commit. mode='files' restores tracked files safely; mode='hard' discards all changes and requires approval.
name: git_revert

mode.description: Restore tracked files (default) or hard reset.

path.description: Repository folder, e.g. 'my-app' for /workspace/my-app. Default: the session's active repository (the first one cloned), or the only repository under /workspace.

reference.description: Checkpoint tag, commit SHA, or ref to restore.

description: Publish the current branch to GitHub: the only way commits leave the sandbox (a raw `git push` is refused). Depending on the organization's signing mode the commits are re-created through GitHub's API so GitHub signs them (local commit hashes then change), or pushed as they are. Commit first; call this before git_open_pr if you only want to publish.
name: git_push

branch.description: Branch to publish (default: the checked-out one).

force_with_lease.description: Allow replacing remote commits you have not fetched (rarely).

path.description: Repository folder, e.g. 'my-app' for /workspace/my-app. Default: the session's active repository (the first one cloned), or the only repository under /workspace.

description: Publish the current branch and open a pull request for it on GitHub.
name: git_open_pr

path.description: Repository folder, e.g. 'my-app' for /workspace/my-app. Default: the session's active repository (the first one cloned), or the only repository under /workspace.

target_branch.description: Base branch to merge into (default: main).

description: Pause execution and wait durably for an external event to complete before continuing: CI status on a pull request ('ci_status'), a pull request review ('review'), a sandbox background process ('process_exit'), or a timer delay ('time'). The turn concludes in a 'waiting' state, yielding resources; when the event occurs, a new continuation turn is automatically woken with the result payload.
name: wait_for

identifier.description: Target identifier: 'owner/repo#123' for ci_status/review, process id for process_exit, or duration in seconds for time.

target.description: The event category to wait for: ci_status, review, process_exit, or time.

timeout_seconds.description: Optional maximum wait timeout in seconds before automatically waking.
